paragraphs.source_en: Eight months had passed in the blink of an eye since the lord of the castle, Matsudaira Motoyasu, had been welcomed home. The people of Okazaki were now neatly and smartly dressed, transformed beyond comparison with former days, and this was not solely because the rice and grain exacted by the people of Sunpu for more than a decade had at last begun to nourish them. After word spread that Motoyasu had returned to Okazaki Castle, vessels of every kind came thronging to the castle town by way of the Yahagi and Sugō rivers, trade flourished, and Okazaki gradually recovered its vitality and prosperity.

paragraphs.source_en: The common people, who had until then resorted to every means of concealing their grain, could finally set their minds at ease. Torii Iga-no-kami contributed the gold, silver, and grain he had accumulated over many years to the restoration of the castle. The battlements everywhere had been renewed, the stone walls restored, and even the roof over the main gate now presented an imposing sight. The castle's complete transformation immediately made it a source of pride to the people of the domain, attracting ever more merchants to trade and bringing steadily growing prosperity to the markets.
